label: Thursday, October 29, 2026 · Delivery-duopoly day edition
intro: Good morning. It's Thursday, October 29th. Here's your Read Daily brief.

items.title: No change in interest rates after last month’s increase
items.take: The Fed held steady Wednesday afternoon after last month’s increase, and Wall Street closed higher for a third straight session. The instant-reaction calls flagged dissents from Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, a reminder the committee is still split on weighing a cooling jobs market against inflation.

items.title: Alphabet stock drops 10% while Microsoft rises after earnings
items.take: Alphabet’s $51.4 billion of capex, up 114%, outran its $42.3 billion of operating cash flow and pushed quarterly free cash flow negative, and the stock fell about 10% premarket, on track for its worst post-earnings reaction ever. Microsoft rose roughly 3% on Azure growth of 48% excluding currency and capex that came in below expectations.

items.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17 billion
items.take: DoorDash announced a roughly $17 billion deal for Instacart, about $65 a share, with the Instacart brand and app staying on. It pairs DoorDash’s restaurant engine with Instacart’s grocery partners and builds a delivery duopoly that regulators will now get to look at.

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO is all about ignoring the future
items.take: With word that as much as 20% of Anthropic’s IPO could be opened to retail investors, Breakingviews argues pricing the deal means largely ignoring the future, the very uncertainty that makes the AI builder’s valuation so contested.

items.title: Anthropic’s plan to protect humanity has a flaw
items.take: The opinion page takes on Anthropic’s governance ahead of the IPO: investors are being asked to trust the founders with the company’s safety mission, and that founder-control structure is the flaw critics keep pointing at.

items.title: The Markets: Why Investors Are Reducing AI Exposure
items.take: This week’s episode digs into why institutional investors are trimming AI exposure right as the IPO calendar, Anthropic included, leans hardest into the theme. A useful counterweight on a morning of AI earnings drama.
